text:
Anna: Heads-up — noticed sustained mem growth on node pool C when running long-context replay (>=64k tokens). KV cache resident set climbs ~1.6GB over 30m and doesn't drop.
Mike: Oh no. Repro script or load profile?
Anna: Repro script attached in gist (https://example.com/repro). It's the longtail chat replay + lots of continuing streams. Allocation profile from pprof shows many ~3-8KB slab allocations pinned in small bins.
Raj: That smells like binning mismatch + fragmentation. Are we seeing lots of partially used blocks (holes)?
Anna: Yes. `kv_slab_stats` shows high free-fragment count across mini-slabs, and `freepool` churn high. Eviction still frees entries but doesn't coalesce small holes fast enough.
Sophie: Do we have a recent kernel change that altered allocation packing? I remember the kernel selection patch last week touched continuous-batching which nudged seq lengths.
Mike: Kernel change is unrelated but workload distribution changed. We did switch batcher to prefer larger batches which increases typical sequence prefix length and KV cache lifetime.
Raj: Proposed quick fix: tune bin sizes to include a 6KB class instead of 4KB/8KB gap — reduces internal fragmentation for 3-7KB items.
Anna: Agree. Also compaction policy: current compactor triggers on wall-clock interval + global fragmentation threshold. Maybe add a per-slab aging trigger: if >X% holes older than T -> compact that slab.
Sophie: Per-slab compaction would be great but we need to measure CPU cost. Compaction has been our main perf budget risk during busy periods.
Mike: What about sampled async compaction: pick a slab with probability proportional to frag-score, recompact N bytes per second budget.
Raj: That aligns with prior notes. Frag-score = free_bytes / slab_bytes * age_factor. Make age_factor = mean_age / (mean_age + tau).
Anna: I ran a micro-experiment: adding a 6KB bin reduced steady-state RSS by ~9% on the replay test, but fragmentation count still high for >16KB objects.
Mike: So we need multi-prong: (1) extra mid-size bins, (2) per-slab async compaction with CPU budget, (3) smarter eviction for long-lived items.
Sophie: For (3) can we promote pin scores based on reuse distance and penalize items that are 1) large and 2) low reuse? Prefer evicting them earlier to reduce holes.
Raj: Yep. Another trick: when evicting a large entry, try to split it into smaller logical entries in the cache if the format allows—not always possible but helps packing.
Anna: Quick config snippet I tested locally for async compaction:

```
kv.compactor.enabled=true
kv.compactor.cpu_budget_ms_per_min=120
kv.compactor.sample_window_secs=30
kv.compactor.frag_score_threshold=0.12
kv.bins.extra_sizes=[6k]
kv.eviction.large_item_penalty=1.5
```

Mike: Nice. How did latency look under that config?
Anna: Latency median unchanged, p95 +5-8ms during compaction windows but within SLO for the test harness. Overall cost dropped slightly due to fewer page faults.
Sophie: Can we add a canary: enable these settings on Dedicated pool only and collect `kv_slab_histogram`, `compaction_cycles`, and `page_faults` metrics?
Raj: Also add a debug trace event for compactor decisions — cheap counter that increments per slab compact attempt, and bucketed time spent.
Mike: I'll wire metrics. Can we gate the per-slab age factor with a circuit breaker so we avoid thrashing on flappy workloads?
Anna: Good call. Add `kv.compactor.circuit_breaker=true` and threshold by compaction_failure_rate.
Sophie: Timeline — who can run a canary tomorrow? Raj you have bandwidth?
Raj: I can run canary on pool D tomorrow morning. Will start with only the 6KB bin + sampling compactor with low budget.
Mike: I'll create a dashboard panel for comparison and hook an alert if p95 latency regresses >15% or RSS reduction <5%.
deploy-bot: build succeeded for `kv/compactor-config` — canary image tagged `kv-compact-canary-20260318`.
Anna: Pushed the canary config to pool D. Will watch metrics and post results here in ~2 hours.
Sophie: If positive, we should draft a short RFC: "adaptive-bin-and-budgeted-compaction" with experiments, perf numbers, and rollback plan.
Anna: Agreed. I'll collect pprof + slab dumps and paste a short summary after the run.
Raj: One last thought — consider using a buddy allocator inside problem slabs: merge adjacent holes opportunistically when doing background compaction to reduce copying.
Mike: That might complicate allocator invariants but worth prototyping in the sim harness first.
Anna: Ok thanks all — will update after canary. TL;DR: extra 6KB bin + sampled async compaction looks promising, CPU cost manageable, p95 small bump during compaction.
Sophie: :thumbsup: keep notes about how it interacts with long-context KV growth (we care about multi-hour tails).
Mike: Thanks — nice debugging loop.
